findings.where: Header nav 'Destinations', the logo home link, and the footer links 'Privacy', 'Terms' and 'Report content'
findings.fault: Every way off this page is a dead end. 'Destinations' goes to an anchor (#destinations) that this page does not have. The logo, Privacy, Terms and Report content all reload this same page. A visitor who wants to look at hostels, read the privacy terms or report something has nowhere to go.
findings.who_objects: The backpacker. Having read why the ranking is fair, they now want to see the hostels in Bali or Lombok, or check the privacy policy before trusting the site. Each click brings them back to the same text. On a page whose whole job is trust, that reads as broken or unfinished.

findings.where: H1 'How we rank' and the intro promise 'how a hostel's position is decided', against the 'Ranking method' section
findings.fault: The page never says what puts one hostel above another. It says what rank does not depend on (payment, partner tier). It says what a score is made of. It never says whether the list is ordered by that score, by distance, or by something else, so the promise in the heading is not kept.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker comparing two Kuta hostels who wants to know why one is listed first. They read the whole page and still can't answer that question, which is the one the page is named for.

findings.fault: The content sits under the wrong headings. 'Ranking method' holds most of the scoring rules: pulling scores toward the area average, which reviews count, the reward-code badge and the 'No reviews yet' state. 'Scoring method' holds only time decay. A reader who jumps to 'Scoring method' to learn how a score works misses most of it.
findings.who_objects: The visitor who skims by heading, which is how most people read a page like this on a phone. They come away thinking a score is only about how recent the reviews are.

findings.where: Body copy throughout, worst in the 'Hostelworld, for comparison' paragraph and the second and third 'Ranking method' paragraphs
findings.fault: The task text is written in long, packed sentences, one of them around 60 words. Terms like 'weighted count of recent reviews', 'partner tier', 'reward-code badge' and 'area average' are never explained. 'Pulled toward the area average' is never shown with an example, such as a hostel with 4 reviews at 9.6 and what it displays.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker in their twenties reading on a phone, maybe in transit. They won't work through dense, legal-sounding prose to see why a score looks the way it does, so the openness the page is proud of doesn't reach them.

findings.where: Intro block: the lead paragraph, the summary sentence and the three-item numbered list, then the first sentence of 'Ranking method'
findings.fault: The opening says the same thing three times at three type sizes: a lead paragraph, a summary sentence, then a list that repeats the summary. 'No hostel can pay for a higher position' then comes back as the first line of the next section. The list is also numbered, which suggests steps in order when these are separate promises.
findings.who_objects: The visitor, who has to read three introductions before any method begins. The repetition makes the page feel padded rather than plain.

findings.where: The pay-for-rank promise ('No hostel can pay for a higher position'), intro list item 1
findings.fault: The page's strongest trust claim is set as list item 1 in small body type. Nothing about it stands out from the lines around it, and the intro paragraph above it is larger than the promise itself.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker used to OTAs where placement is bought. The single line that would reassure them most is the easiest one to skim past.

findings.where: Closing section 'Hostelworld, for comparison', the last content on the page
findings.fault: The page ends on a named competitor, with a long cited sentence about Hostelworld's review windows. It never says plainly what Manta does differently or why that helps the traveller. The project's positioning keeps its demand-side claims free of competitor names and stays out of Hostelworld's ground, so ending here reads as a jab rather than help.
findings.who_objects: The visitor, who wanted to know how to read Manta's scores and instead gets a footnote about another site's help centre. The founder too, since a Hostelworld affiliate application is pending and the positioning is built to name no competitor.

findings.where: End of the main content, above the footer, at both widths
findings.fault: After the method there is no next step: no link to destinations or hostels. The page simply stops into blank sand space and the footer.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who is now convinced the ranking is fair and wants to start looking where to stay. They have to scroll back up to the nav, where 'Destinations' doesn't work anyway.

findings.where: Whole page at desktop (overview): one narrow text column hard left, the right two-thirds empty, no illustration or brand moment
findings.fault: On desktop the page is a narrow grey column of text against a large empty field. No visual hierarchy or brand element breaks it up. It reads like a terms-of-service page, not the effortless, beachy brand the rest of the site promises, and the empty right side looks unfinished rather than calm.
findings.who_objects: The backpacker, whose first feeling should be 'effortless'. A wall of text says 'small print'. The brand also names sterile and corporate as its enemy, which this page is.

findings.where: Whole page copy, against the footer line 'Launching across Indonesia · piloting now in Bali'
findings.fault: The method is written in the present tense as if it were already ranking live reviews ('Every review that passes our checks counts…'). The page never says the site is pre-launch with no reviews yet, or when the method was published or last changed. The visitor can't tell whether this describes something running now. Lombok, half of this visitor's trip, is not mentioned anywhere.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor who goes looking for these scores and finds none, or finds Lombok uncovered. The present-tense claims then read as overstated, on the one page meant to earn trust.

findings.fault: The footer wordmark is coloured like the nav's home link but does nothing when clicked. Visitors expect a footer logo to take them home.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who clicks it to get back to the start and nothing happens. It's a small dead end on top of the broken links.
